verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe a single desktop workspace where you can launch work, track progress across multiple agents, review changes, and merge results. They also describe a centralized control page for jumping between agent sessions and checking progress. Multi-agent task assignment, including third-party agents, is documented as well. missing for 10: in-depth documentation beyond brief marketing statements, independent or hands-on corroboration of the unified session-management workspace.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can manage multiple agent-driven coding sessions from one unified workspace

citations.quote: Launch work from GitHub, track progress across multiple agents, review changes, and merge completed work—all from one desktop workspace built natively on GitHub.
Use one centralized control page to jump between agent sessions, check progress, and stay in control without losing your place.
Assign tasks to agents like Copilot, Claude by Anthropic, and OpenAI Codex, and let them plan, explore, and execute work autonomously in the background.
enforce governance by managing agents from a single control plane
